Design direction: what's most characteristic of the subject? A Breakout game — the playfield itself should be the hero, not a generic headline block. So the canvas/arcade cabinet framing is the entry point. Think arcade cabinet aesthetic — CRT scanlines, chunky arcade type. A near-black background with a single neon accent would read as the obvious arcade cliché, so I want a richer palette. Let me think of a distinctive palette: maybe a warm dusk palette — deep plum/ink background with a spread of colored blocks (a full multi-hue block palette is inherent to Breakout itself). Use a bold display face like "Bungee" or "Rubik Mono One" or "Archivo Black" paired with a readable body like "IBM Plex Sans" or "Space Grotesk". Japanese text needed too — so a JP font like "Zen Kaku Gothic New" or "Noto Sans JP" for body, and for display maybe "Bungee" (Latin only) for numbers/labels plus a Japanese display like "RocknRoll One" or "DotGothic16" — DotGothic16 is a pixel/arcade-ish Japanese font, very characteristic of arcade games! That's a great fit: DotGothic16 for display (pixel arcade, supports Japanese), and "Zen Kaku Gothic New" or "IBM Plex Sans JP" for body. Palette idea: deep ink navy #10141f base with layered subtle grid + soft radial glows in multiple hues (not just one accent). Block colors: a spread of coral, amber, aqua, lime, magenta, cyan. Paddle in warm cream. Ball in white with glow. Layout: an asymmetric layout — left column with the game cabinet, right column with a "console" panel: score, level, lives, combo meter, power-up legend, controls, high score, stats. Plus a top bar with the title in huge pixel type and a marquee. Features to make it feel alive: - Canvas game with real physics: paddle, ball, blocks with hit points (multi-hit blocks with color changes), particle bursts on break, screen shake, combo counter, power-ups (multi-ball, wide paddle, slow ball, laser?, extra life), levels with different patterns, brick patterns. - Ball trail, glow, squash on paddle hit. - Paddle control: mouse, touch, keyboard arrows, and pointer. - Score popups floating. - Level clear transition. - Sound via WebAudio (blips) with mute toggle — nice arcade touch. - CRT scanline overlay + vignette on canvas, subtle. - HUD with animated numbers. - Combo meter bar. - Start overlay with instructions, pause, game over screen. - Micro-interactions: buttons with hover, key hints, panel reveals on scroll (IntersectionObserver), marquee ticker. - Ambient background: animated subtle drifting dot grid + soft light pools, maybe faint moving "brick" motif in background. Keep tasteful and performant. Let me plan the code carefully. Structure: ```html meta, title, fonts (Google Fonts: DotGothic16, Zen Kaku Gothic New, maybe Bungee for numerals)
layered: grid, glow pools, drifting bricks (CSS animated divs)

Standard approach: ```js function hitBrick(b, br){ const nx = clamp(b.x, br.x, br.x+br.w); const ny = clamp(b.y, br.y, br.y+br.h); const dx = b.x-nx, dy=b.y-ny; if(dx*dx+dy*dy > b.r*b.r) return false; // resolve: use overlap const overlapX = (br.w/2 + b.r) - Math.abs(b.x - (br.x+br.w/2)); const overlapY = (br.h/2 + b.r) - Math.abs(b.y - (br.y+br.h/2)); if(overlapX < overlapY){ b.vx = -b.vx; b.x += Math.sign(b.x-(br.x+br.w/2))*overlapX; } else { b.vy = -b.vy; b.y += Math.sign(b.y-(br.y+br.h/2))*overlapY; } return true; } ``` Only one brick per substep per ball (break after hit) — good enough and prevents weirdness.
